newsitem.title: UK: Abbey National extends post-results rally.
newsitem.headline: Abbey National extends post-results rally.

text.p: Shares in British bank Abbey National Plc extended their post-results rally in midsession trade on Tuesday as investors shrugged off signs of a difficult mortgage market and focused on healthy headline profit growth.

The shares slipped in the immediate aftermath of the results, hit by disappointment about the size of the dividend and worries about market share erosion and margin pressure in the bank's mortgage business.
But optimism about Abbey National's non-mortgage business, as well as general strength in the banking sector, helped lead its shares up 35p to 845 by 1036 GMT, compared with an early low of 789-3/4.
"The big picture is that the mortgage market is becoming increasingly competitive and you can see that reflected in their margins and their volume performance," UBS analyst John Aitken said.
"That probably augurs badly for players with a heavy involvement in mortgages. But Abbey has the advantage of having a fairly strong non-mortgage stream of business," he said.
"While we retain some reservations about the future profitability of the mortgage market, we still think that Abbey is a relatively good value stock in a sector that looks pretty expensive."
Half-year pre-tax profits rose 23 percent to 687 million stg, after a charge of 67 million relating to changes in the proposed rate of corporation tax. The interim dividend was 10.2 pence.

"There are a few disappointments in there but overall the figures were fairly good and Abbey could still be a bid target," one market-maker said. "The results were reasonable, although not brilliant."
Analysts had forecast profits between 673 and 700 million and a dividend of between 10.2 and 10.5 pence.

"Although the numbers overall look okay, I think the dividend will be perceived as disappointing," said Panmure Gordon analyst David Poutney. "People were looking for an increase of 20 percent and it's gone up 17. Given that their tier 1 ratio has gone up from 8.5 to 9.2, that's disappointing."

Abbey National's market share of UK mortgages was estimated at 14.3 percent at June 30, up from 12.1 percent at the half-year stage the previous year but down from the full-year 1996 figure of 14.7 percent.
Poutney pointed out that margins were being squeezed.
"Margins are under pressure, although there's no great surprise there," he said. "So there's margin pressure plus loss of market share."

The strength in Abbey National shares was mirrored across the sector. While Abbey was the biggest gainer among the major bank shares in percentage terms, Lloyds TSB Group Plc and National Westminster Bank also gained strongly.
Lloyds was 17p firmer at 663-1/2 and NatWest gained 22p to 862-1/2.
Barclays Plc firmed 12-1/2p to 12.33-1/2 stg, HSBC Holdings Plc gained 24-1/2p to 21.45 stg and Standard Chartered Plc climbed seven to 971-1/2p.
